text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — I skimmed the batcher refactor and want to lock down the hedging + eviction interface before we ship. High level issue: small/short requests are getting latency-regressed when we favour pack-and-wait. Thoughts?
ken: I saw that in staging traces. Short requests wait ~6–8ms extra when the microcoalesce window is 4ms. If we hedge aggressively we increase wasted GPU cycles.
jasper: Tradeoff summary I sketched earlier: hedging reduces tail for tiny requests but raises cost (more queued microbatches). We need a signal to prefer hedging only when queue length < N or when tenant historic-latency > SLO.
oliver: Could we use a per-tenant fastpath hint? e.g., tenant metadata `prefer-low-latency: true` and route to a tiny-window lane with reserved headroom. That avoids global policy churn.
sophie: Is headroom per-tenant feasible without blowing up memory because of KV cache pressure? If we keep tiny lanes we fragment KV cache on the GPU and cause thrash.
maria: Exactly — the KVC cache thrash is the main worry. Suggestion: split eviction strategy into (1) soft-reserve for fastpath (cheap metadata only) and (2) borrow-on-demand for KV pages with a cooldown.
ken: How about an eviction lease protocol: tiny-lane can request a short lease (20ms) on a subset of KV segments. If lease denied, it hedges by sending requests immediately (no batching). If granted, it coalesces as usual.
jasper: That sounds workable. We need to define the lease API in the runtime: `request_lease(tenant, segments, ttl_ms)` -> {granted: bool, granted_segments: []}. Keep it idempotent and cheap.
oliver: Two concerns: (a) overhead: extra round trips in admission path, (b) fairness: long-running tenants might starve tiny tenants by holding leases.
sophie: For fairness: enforce lease caps and an LRU-style reclaim with priority weights. Also add a telemetry counter `lease_denied_by_tenant` to track abuse.
maria: Ops question — what happens during node failover? If leases are lost, tiny-lane must gracefully fall back to immediate hedging. No hard failures.
ken: Agreed. Fallback behavior should be explicit: `if lease_lost -> switch to immediate hedging; emit event lease_fallback` so Console can alert.
jasper: Implementation plan outline: 1) proto for lease request + response; 2) runtime in-memory lease manager per GPU process; 3) admission path hook that queries lease manager; 4) telemetry and dashboards.
maria: Rollout plan: start with heuristic-only mode (no lease grants) to gather traces; then enable leases for 10% of traffic for low-risk tenants.
oliver: Also add a toggle to allow dedicated pools to bypass lease negotiation entirely (Dedicated customers get pinning).
sophie: One more tradeoff: KBW (keep-busy-writes) when a tiny-lane hedges will increase KV miss rates. We should measure miss amplification and maybe add write-back cooldown.
jasper: For the API boundary: keep the lease proto internal to runtime. Expose only two high-level flags in the public admission API: `latency_preference` and `lease_opt_in`. That keeps operator surface minimal.
maria: Nice. Can someone sketch the proto and a short telemetry plan? If we agree I'll open a PR with the proto + a small sim harness.
ken: I'll draft the proto and a quick sim that replays staging traces and reports cost/latency deltas.
jasper: I'll wire up the telemetry counters and add a Console dashboard mockup.
deploy-bot: deploy-batcher-refactor/branch -> staging succeeded (build #4521) :rocket:
maria: Thanks — let's reconvene after the sim results. :thumbsup:
